title: pariññeyya sutta
credit: Pāḷi text and English translation as in Mor’s Pāḷi Workshop booklet.

paras.en:
“Bhikkhus, there are these Four Noble Truths.
What four? The noble truth of dukkha, the noble truth of the origin of dukkha, the noble truth of the cessation of dukkha, the noble truth of the way leading to the cessation of dukkha.
These are the Four Noble Truths.

And what, bhikkhus, is the noble truth that is to be fully understood? The noble truth of dukkha is to be fully understood; the noble truth of the origin of dukkha is to be abandoned; the noble truth of the cessation of dukkha is to be realized;
the noble truth of the way leading to the cessation of dukkha is to be developed.

Therefore, bhikkhus, an exertion should be made to understand: ‘This is dukkha.’ An exertion should be made to understand: ‘This is the origin of dukkha.’
An exertion should be made to understand:
‘This is the cessation of dukkha.’
An exertion should be made to understand:
‘This is the way leading to the cessation of dukkha.’”
